definitions.explanation: The second son born in a family. In traditional Japanese family structure, the second son typically did not inherit the household, unlike the eldest son.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{三|さん}{人|にん}{兄弟|きょうだい}の{次男|じなん}だ。
examples.english: He is the second son of three brothers.

examples.japanese: {次男|じなん}は{来年|らいねん}{小学校|しょうがっこう}に{入|はい}る。
examples.english: Our second son will enter elementary school next year.

examples.japanese: {昔|むかし}は{長男|ちょうなん}が{家|いえ}を{継|つ}ぎ、{次男|じなん}は{独立|どくりつ}するのが{一般的|いっぱんてき}だった。
examples.english: In the past, the eldest son would inherit the household, and the second son would strike out on his own.

notes:
{次男|じなん} means second son. Part of the Japanese birth-order system that is commonly used in daily life, official documents, and family registers ({戸籍|こせき}).

BIRTH ORDER - SONS:
- {長男|ちょうなん}: eldest son
- {次男|じなん}: second son
- {三男|さんなん}: third son

BIRTH ORDER - DAUGHTERS:
- {長女|ちょうじょ}: eldest daughter
- {次女|じじょ}: second daughter
- {三女|さんじょ}: third daughter

CULTURAL NOTE:
In traditional Japanese families, the {長男|ちょうなん} often bears special responsibilities like inheriting the family home and caring for elderly parents. The {次男|じなん} historically had more freedom. This distinction has weakened in modern times but still influences family dynamics.
